name: The Quanta We Owed: Debt Testimonials 2195-2214
creator: Collective authorship, edited by Tomás Osei-Lindqvist
description: A zine-turned-contraband-anthology collecting first-person testimonials from Tier 1 and Tier 2 residents about corponation debt — augmentation financing traps, housing credit collapse, medical chrome repossession. The text is raw and unedited, preserving the mixed creole dialects and BCI-transcribed speech patterns of its contributors. Physical copies are hand-stapled on salvaged paper and distributed through Shelf networks; a pirate neural-feed version circulates on encrypted channels.
medium: physical zine (Shelf distribution) and pirate neural-feed download
cultural_impact: Became the primary organizing text for the Meridian Debt Jubilee movement of 2216, read aloud at protests and smuggled into Tier 3 neighborhoods. Several corponations named in the testimonials successfully lobbied for its suppression under the Meridian Compact's defamation statutes.
controversy: Three contributing authors were served with corporate defamation injunctions. One, a woman identified only as 'Fatou from the 14th Shelf,' disappeared six weeks after the physical edition began circulating. Her absence is noted in handwritten marginalia in many copies.
story_hooks: A Tier 4 journalist acquires a physical copy and begins tracking down contributors, only to realize the investigation is being monitored by the corponation named most frequently in the testimonials.
A numbered first-edition copy surfaces in a Spire estate sale — someone powerful was keeping tabs on this text long before it was banned.
Tomás Osei-Lindqvist has been in hiding since 2216 and wants to publish a follow-up volume, but needs someone to carry the testimonials out of the Shelf.
